devotions.titel: Arise and Come Away With Him
devotions.citaat: God says, come away from what you think you have to protect. Come away with me. Trust in me, he says.

zinnen.tekst: I want to tell you about a prophetic word that I got a little while ago for our church. ... We went to a marriage retreat, not because our marriage is a mess, but because we don't want our marriage to be a mess. ... The woman, she's a minister of the gospel. And she had a prophetic word for us. She said it's not one that she's, in all her years, she's never given a word like this before. ... And she said, this is a word for you. And as she was speaking it, I said, yes, that is for us. This is for our church. ... And what she was saying is the verse in that that stood out to her the most was, The season has changed. The bondage of your barren winter has ended.

And so I want to take us through this passage of scripture. ... The first thing I see is it says, arise. Go with God. Verse 10, the one I love calls to me, arise, my dearest. Hurry, my darling. Come away with me. ... And he's calling us to arise. Arise. Arise from what? I believe he's calling us to arise from the disappointments. Arise from the pain of your past. Arise from your heartache. Arise from your fear. Arise from hiding in your comfort. Arise from hiding from risk. Arise from hiding from protecting parts of your life from God. Arise to stand in the fullness of who you are in God. To arise in the fullness of all that He has for you, the life that He has for you, the life that He's called you to live. Come away with me, he says. Come to the higher place, he says.

Yes, he's our loving Father in heaven, but he's also the one that sits on the throne. He's the most powerful being. ... It's time to put our trust in Him. He who loves you. He who loves us. To live our lives with God. Away from trusting in our feelings. Away from trusting in our abilities to living by the Spirit of God, away from protecting our hearts from what if God doesn't come through, away from I've got to look after myself, I've got to look after my family, I've got to look after my future, I've got to look after my finances. God says, come away from what you think you have to protect. Come away with me. Trust in me, he says. Let me look after you. Let me look after your future. Let me look after your family. Let me look after your finances. We see in the Old Testament, Abram being asked to come away from the place of his past. ... And when he did that, it changed the world. I wonder what's at stake for us. ... And today I believe God is asking us to come away with him. ... I wonder what's on the other side of our obedience, of our trust, of us saying, hey, I'm going to put my life in his hands. I'm going to live his way. Maybe you've had a season of holding on to your past, but today God's calling us to arise. Come away with him. ... He's like, hurry, do it now, do it today. Now, now, now is the time.

gebed.tekst: Yes, Lord, we're here to behold You, to gather in Your name, to bring our focus and attention to who You are and what You've done. Well, what a privilege that we get to live in relationship with you when we don't deserve it. What an opportunity we have to share that with people that we know and love, Lord, that they too can live the life that they were created for. Lord, I pray that as we gather together, as we come around your word, Lord, that you would breathe on your word. ... Lord, that you speak into our hearts, into our lives, in Jesus' name. Amen.

devotions.bijbelvers: The one I love calls to me, arise, my dearest. Hurry, my darling. Come away with me. I have come as you have asked to draw you to my heart and to lead you out. For now is the time, my beautiful one.

vraag.tekst: What are you still protecting from Him, and what would it look like to let Him look after it today?

deel.begin: I want to tell you about a prophetic word that I got a little while ago for our church.
deel.oplossing: Away from trusting in our feelings. Away from trusting in our abilities to living by the Spirit of God, away from protecting our hearts from what if God doesn't come through, away from I've got to look after myself, I've got to look after my family, I've got to look after my future, I've got to look after my finances. God says, come away from what you think you have to protect. Come away with me. Trust in me, he says. Let me look after you. Let me look after your future. Let me look after your family. Let me look after your finances.

devotions.titel: He Has Come, As We Asked
devotions.citaat: We've prayed for the presence of God. We've prayed for the Holy Spirit. God has answered the prayer.

zinnen.tekst: Number three, I see here that we can live in answered prayer. The one I love calls to me, arise, my dearest. Hurry, my darling. Come away with me, he says. I have come as you have asked. I have come as you have asked to draw you to my heart and lead you out. Church, we've prayed, haven't we? We've prayed for the presence of God. We've prayed for the Holy Spirit. God has answered the prayer. He's come to draw us to his heart, to lead us out from living in accordance with our flesh, our own abilities, our feelings to live a higher way. He's come. But what does it mean to live in answered prayer? What does it mean to live in response to Him actually having come, having done what we've asked Him to do? How do we live? What is our expectation?

You know, there's a story in the book of Acts of Peter when he was kept in prison. The church was earnestly praying for God to get him, to bring him out. ... Acts chapter 12, verse 11. Peter came to himself and said, Now I know without a doubt that the Lord has sent an angel and he's rescued me from Herod's clutches ... Miraculously, he got out of prison. ... Peter knocked on the outer entrance and a servant named Rhoda came to answer the door. And when she recognized Peter's voice, she was so overjoyed, she ran back without opening it and explained, Peter's at the door. Can you imagine? They've been praying that God would get him out of prison. And now Peter's at the door. Answered prayer. So how did the church respond? Did they say, praise God. He answered our prayer. This is how they responded. You're out of your mind. ... But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astonished. Guys, God answered their prayer. How do we respond to God answering our prayers?

Think about the story of blind Bartimaeus, this guy who'd been begging on the streets. That's how he made his income. Jesus came past. He said, Jesus, son of God, have mercy on me. Jesus healed him. He could no longer beg. Now he had to work for a living. How do you live in answered prayer? ... Think of the people in the Old Testament of God who left Egypt through the wilderness to the promised land. They were getting manna from heaven, free food every day. They get into the promised land, the manna stops. Now you've got people to defeat. You've got to start farming. Hey, if God's answered our prayer, what are we going to do? How are we going to respond? We've got a city to reach. We've got a nation to reach. ... Oh, the Holy Spirit turned up in the service. That was nice. God answered our prayer. We're seeing people come in through the doors and come into our church. That was really nice. Well, how are we going to live in the answered prayer? Are we going to take ownership, take responsibility and say, God is moving. We're going to be part of this. What team can we serve on? ... How do we live in answered prayer?

Lord, I pray that as we gather together, as we come around your word, Lord, that you would breathe on your word. ... Lord, that you speak into our hearts, into our lives, in Jesus' name. Amen.

vraag.tekst: How do we live in answered prayer?

punt.tekst: We can live in answered prayer.

devotions.titel: A New Season, Into His Light
devotions.citaat: Bring whatever is in the darkness in your heart into the light. The season of hiding things is over.

zinnen.tekst: Number four, it's a new season. Verse 11, the season has changed. The season has changed. It's not going to change. It's not in the midst of changing. The season has changed. Now, I know physically it's changing and it's getting colder. Rode my bike yesterday and thought I should have worn gloves. Maybe I'm getting soft. Maybe the season's changing. But the season that he's talking about here is a spiritual season. And he's saying it's not changing. It's not in the midst of change. It has changed. We are now in a new season.

They were full of this passion and vision for a project that they're working on. A year ago, two years ago, even six months ago, this wasn't happening. People weren't full of passion and energy. ... We're now in a new season. We're in a new season. Let's not live like we're still in winter where fruitfulness is lacking. Spring comes after summer. New shoots, new buds, newness. New Christians, new team members, new leaders. It's a new season. Sorry, I'm just excited. We're in a new season, church. ... When you think about our church, I want to encourage you, don't be thinking about a past season. Think about the current season and the vision that's ahead. When it comes to what God has for your life, let's let go of the past disappointments and the pains. Let's let go of those things that would hold us back. Let's come and arise and go with God. Let's arise to a higher place. Let's do this God's way, not man's way.

The season of hiding is over. And I think he's talking about our hearts. Where there is pain or where there is fear in our hearts, it stops us from being wholehearted. Wholehearted in how we live, wholehearted in how we follow Jesus. Forgiveness, clean hearts, pure hearts, free from resentment, free from bitterness, free from disappointments. Bring that into the light. Bring whatever is in the darkness in your heart into the light. The season of hiding things is over. Bring it into the light. Let God deal with it. Let God deal with what's going on.

gebed.tekst: Yes, Lord, we're here to behold You, to gather in Your name, to bring our focus and attention to who You are and what You've done. Well, what a privilege that we get to live in relationship with you when we don't deserve it. What an opportunity we have to share that with people that we know and love, Lord, that they too can live the life that they were created for. Lord, I pray that as we gather together, as we come around your word, Lord, that you would breathe on your word. ... Lord, that you speak into our hearts, into our lives, in Jesus' name. Amen.

devotions.bijbelvers: The season has changed. The bondage of your barren winter has ended and the season of hiding is over and gone.

vraag.tekst: What is in the darkness of your heart that you can bring into His light today?

devotions.citaat: So Jesus came on mission, on mission to restore us back to our purpose, to our relationship with God.

zinnen.tekst: God has us on the planet for a reason. He created us for a reason. When it comes to purpose, our purpose is what God created. It's the reason God created us. We haven't all got different purposes. There's one purpose that God created us for. The Bible speaks about it. There's different aspects to it. There's a relationship with God that we would carry his glory, that we would live life. Now, we stepped away from all of that and we lost it as humanity. So Jesus came on mission, on mission to restore us back to our purpose, to our relationship with God. And then he said, now I'm handing you, it's tag. Now you are part of the mission. I'm entrusting you with the mission. I've done the hard part. Now I'm going back to the Father. I'm going to send you the Holy Spirit so you continue with the mission. And I have a plan. And the plan is the church.

We put our whole heart into what God's called us to be part of, the mission, his plan. He only has one plan, the church. So we put our whole heart into that plan, into the mission. Yes, we get disappointed by things. Yes, we get disappointed by people. Yes, we get disappointed by situations. Yes, we can get disappointed by the church itself. But God allows us to be bigger and to live as overcomers in Christ Jesus. You know, one of the things of the past season has been a pandemic that we in our lifetime had never seen before. It caused us to be locked up in our homes. It made many of our worlds smaller. But it's time to open up our lives again. ... It's like it's our social muscle got weakened. Well, it's time to strengthen it. It's time to strengthen it. It's time to go with God. Take the higher way.

Let me tell you why you're here. You're here to be salt seasoning that brings out the God flavors of this earth. If you lose your saltiness, how will people taste godliness? ... You're here to be light, bringing out the God colors in the world. God's not a secret to be kept. We're going public with this, as public as a city on a hill. ... Now that I've put you there on a hilltop, on a light stand, shine. Keep open house. Be generous with your lives. ... And by opening up to others, you'll prompt people to open up with God, this generous Father in heaven. Maybe it's time that some of us open up our homes and host Connect groups. Maybe it's time that some of us said, you know what, I'm going to make sure that not a single person walks through the door without being welcomed into the house of God. I'm going to represent Jesus to people. I'm going to play my part in his plan.

gebed.tekst: Yes, Lord, we're here to behold You, to gather in Your name, to bring our focus and attention to who You are and what You've done. zinnen.tekst: Number six, choose joy. Listen to this. The rains have soaked the earth and left it bright with blossoming flowers. This season for singing and pruning the vines has arrived. There's a spiritual hunger in the world. ... There's also a spiritual hunger in Amsterdam, in Brussels. Bright, blossoming flowers. Think of those as people. Do we see them? ... Are we inviting them in to play their part in all that God's called them to, to play their part in God's plan? It's a season for singing and for pruning. Singing. What's our attitude today? Are we singing about what we're part of? Are we singing about the salvations? Are we singing about the miracles? You know, I don't know how many of you guys were here in the afternoon service two weeks ago. We had a Holy Spirit weekend. God moved in this service. ... At the end of that service, the end of the afternoon service, I stood here on this platform. ... Then I asked people, who has been physically healed? Not just hoping to be healed, you have been healed in this service. Hands went up. There must have been around 30 people who put their hands up. God's on the move. God's doing something. ... Are we singing about all that God is doing? Are we part of it?

When I was a teenager, and in my late teens, I was going to university, and at that stage, I wasn't a Christian. I hadn't encountered the reality of who God is. But I wanted my life to mean something. And I was doing these self-help courses, personal development programs. And there's this one statement that really stuck with me and has stuck with me even till today. And the statement was this. Someone said, I forget who it was that said this, but they said, he was an older person. And he said, what I've realized over the years is that people are generally about as happy as they make up their mind to be. And sometimes when I'm maybe going through one of my moods, one of my attitudes, or maybe just sad or disappointed about things that are going on, I remember that statement. And it's amazing how quickly your attitude can change. The reality of the fact that most people probably are. There's circumstances and situations which go beyond all of this. But I think most people are about as happy as they make up their mind to be. And you know the will of God. The Bible tells us that his will in 1 Thessalonians chapter 5 is to rejoice always. It's to rejoice always, to pray continually and give thanks in all circumstances that this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus. Singing and pruning, pruning those branches of our lives that aren't godly. Rejoicing about all that God is doing and pruning those things that are not of God in our lives. It's time to sing and prune as we arise and come away with God today.

Then my last point, point seven, is allow the Holy Spirit to fill the atmosphere of your life. The doves in the Bible often are symbolic of the Holy Spirit. It says, I hear the cooing of doves in our land, filling the air with songs to awaken you and guide you forth. This is what the Holy Spirit does. Can you not discern this new day of destiny breaking around you, breaking forth around you? The Holy Spirit filling the atmosphere to awaken us and to guide us forth. ... It's not about the manifestations. It's about getting to know Him. It's knowing Him. ... The Holy Spirit's breathing on what's happening in our church. Can you not discern this new day of destiny breaking forth around you? This is the prophetic word for our church. A prophetic word for every one of us as we step into our destiny, as we step into our future.

To live God's way, to live in the fullness, wholeheartedly, full of freedom and full of joy on the inside. Overcoming the situations and the circumstances that we find ourselves in. Recognizing that there's a spiritual hunger in our church. There's a spiritual hunger in the world that we live. And God has entrusted us with his good news. He's entrusted us with the message of salvation. He's entrusted us to show people what he's like through our lives. Let's take a moment just to let God do what he wants to do and for us to make decisions ourselves. To arise. Arise.

delen.titel: Arise and Come Away With Him
delen.citaat: I believe he's calling us to arise from the disappointments. Arise from the pain of your past. Arise from your heartache.
delen.uitleg: The speaker opens with a prophetic word he received at a marriage retreat: Song of Songs 2:10–13 in the Passion Translation, which he takes as a word for the church. The first thing he sees in it is arise, go with God: arise from disappointment, from the pain of the past, from fear, and from protecting parts of your life from God. God is a loving Father and also the one who sits on the throne, so it is time to put our trust in Him and come away from what we think we have to protect. He reads Genesis 12:1–3, where Abram is asked to come away from the place of his past, and wonders what is on the other side of our obedience. He adds the urgency of the verse: hurry, do it now, do it today.
delen.vraag: Where do you find it hard to trust Him, and what would it look like to come away with Him there?

delen.titel: He Has Come, As We Asked
delen.citaat: Are we going to take ownership, take responsibility and say, God is moving. We're going to be part of this.
delen.uitleg: From the words I have come as you have asked, the speaker says we can live in answered prayer: the church prayed for God's presence and for the Holy Spirit, and God has answered. He reads Acts 12:11 and the scene at the door, where the praying church does not believe that Peter has really been set free. Blind Bartimaeus, healed by Jesus, could no longer beg and had to work; when Israel entered the promised land the manna stopped. So he asks how we respond to answered prayer: take ownership, be part of what God is doing, and serve.
delen.vraag: Where has He already answered a prayer in your life, and how are you living in that answer?

delen.titel: A New Season, Into His Light
delen.citaat: The season of hiding things is over. Bring it into the light. Let God deal with it.
delen.uitleg: Verse 11 says the season has changed: not changing, not about to change, it has changed. He sees it in people who are full of passion and vision that was not there a year ago, and calls the church not to live as if it is still winter: new Christians, new team members, new leaders. Then he turns to freedom: the season of hiding is over, and he thinks that is about our hearts. Pain and fear keep us from following Jesus wholeheartedly, so bring whatever is in the darkness into the light and let God deal with it.
delen.vraag: What have you been hiding, and what would it mean to bring it into His light and let God deal with it?

delen.citaat: I've done the hard part. Now I'm going back to the Father. I'm going to send you the Holy Spirit so you continue with the mission.
delen.uitleg: The speaker says God created us for one purpose: a relationship with Him, carrying His glory. Humanity lost that, so Jesus came on mission to restore us to that relationship, did the hard part, and entrusted the mission to us with the Holy Spirit; His one plan is the church. We get disappointed, even by the church, but God lets us live as overcomers in Christ Jesus. He reads Matthew 5:13–16 from The Message: be salt and light, keep open house, be generous with your lives. He asks whether it is time to open our homes for connect groups and to represent Jesus to people.
delen.vraag: Jesus has done the hard part. How does that change the way you take your part in His mission?

delen.citaat: It's not about the manifestations. It's about getting to know Him. It's knowing Him.
delen.uitleg: Point six is to choose joy. There is a spiritual hunger in the world. He asks us to think of the blossoming flowers in the passage as people, and whether we see those who would be willing to serve God if we only gave them the chance. The season is for singing and pruning. He recalls the Holy Spirit weekend two weeks earlier, when around thirty people said they had been physically healed, and asks whether we are singing about what God is doing. Next to a line from his pre-Christian years, that people are about as happy as they make up their mind to be, with his own note that some circumstances go beyond this, he sets God's will in 1 Thessalonians 5: rejoice always, pray continually, give thanks in all circumstances, in Christ Jesus. Point seven is to let the Holy Spirit fill the atmosphere of your life: it is not about manifestations but about getting to know Him.
delen.vraag: What is He doing around you right now that you could sing about, and what is He asking you to prune?

delen.citaat: Let's leave the past in the past. Let's free ourselves from hiding in the pain and disappointments.
delen.uitleg: The speaker gathers the message and calls everyone to their feet: arise, leave the past in the past, the day of hiding is over, and decide today to live God's way, because God has entrusted us with his good news and with showing people what he is like through our lives. He closes by leaving room for the Holy Spirit to work and for everyone to make their own decisions.
delen.vraag: He has entrusted you with His good news. What would it mean for you to arise and go with Him today?

luister.citaat: The season has changed. It's not going to change. It's not in the midst of changing. The season has changed.

uitnodiging.tekst: The speaker ends by calling everyone to arise and make their own decision. After the message, the host invites anyone who has never put their trust in Jesus, or who has walked away from Him, to make that decision and to pray it together.
uitnodiging.citaat: So let's decide today to live God's way, to step into the fullness of all that God has for us.

gebedspunten.tekst: Thank You, Jesus, that You came on mission to restore us to our relationship with God, and that You have done the hard part.
Lord, we prayed and You have come as we asked. Show us how to live in answered prayer and take our part in what You are doing.
Holy Spirit, fill the atmosphere of our lives. Help us bring into the light what we have been hiding, and to arise and go with God in this new season.

Abram asked to come away from the place of his past; all peoples blessed through his step of faith
the church prays for Peter in prison and does not believe its own answered prayer
the story of blind Bartimaeus, healed by Jesus and no longer able to beg (told, reference not given)

gebed.tekst: Yes, Lord, we're here to behold You, to gather in Your name, to bring our focus and attention to who You are and what You've done. Well, what a privilege that we get to live in relationship with you when we don't deserve it. What an opportunity we have to share that with people that we know and love, Lord, that they too can live the life that they were created for. Lord, I pray that as we gather together, as we come around your word, Lord, that you would breathe on your word. ... Lord, that you speak into our hearts, into our lives, in Jesus' name. Amen.

gebeden.tekst: Yes, Lord, we're here to behold You, to gather in Your name, to bring our focus and attention to who You are and what You've done. Well, what a privilege that we get to live in relationship with you when we don't deserve it. What an opportunity we have to share that with people that we know and love, Lord, that they too can live the life that they were created for. Lord, I pray that as we gather together, as we come around your word, Lord, that you would breathe on your word, Lord, that you'd anoint myself, you'd anoint these words and, Lord, divide them up into what every one of us needs to hear. Lord, that you speak into our hearts, into our lives, in Jesus' name. Amen.

Dear Jesus, thank you for who you are and for what you've done for me. Thank you that you died on the cross for me. And on the third day, you rose again, proving who you are. Thank you that my sins are forgiven and that I can live my life for you. And today I decide to follow you for the rest of my life. In Jesus' name, amen, amen, amen.

So Lord God, right now I pray for those as we are in this new season that you've given us. God, I pray for those who are maybe still worried about things from the past. Maybe there's still things that we're holding on to from the past. Maybe there's still things that we're holding on to from a previous season. In Jesus' name, God, I pray for freedom. In Jesus' name, God, I pray that chains will be broken. In Jesus' name, God, I pray that healing will take place, that breakthrough will take place, that as we are in this new season, Lord God, I pray in Jesus' name that we step boldly, full of courage, full of faith into this new season that we're riding right now. So Lord God, I pray that this is a moment for healing, that this is a moment of restoration, that this is a moment of a new beginning as we step into all that you have for us. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

Lord God, we thank you for who you are. God, we thank you for the people in the world that you placed us in the world. And God, we pray for their salvation. God, our friends, our colleagues, family members. Lord God, we pray that this week you will give us divine opportunities to talk about your grace and your goodness. And we believe you for their salvation in Jesus' name. And Lord God, I pray that this week you will go before us. We pray your blessing over this week. In Jesus' name we pray. ... Amen, amen, amen.
